title: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management: SMAPE accuracy and AI explanations for Demand planning forecasts
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing requirement, access controls and qualified row-level security statements are supported. Minor corrections would complete the background Copilot setting path and add a source for the plain-language SMAPE definition.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Demand planning version 1.4 introduces a calculation accuracy page for forecast time series.
claims.quote:
Demand planning version 1.4 introduces the following new features:

- **Forecast calculation accuracy analysis** – The new calculation accuracy page for forecast time series

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The calculation accuracy page shows the forecasting algorithm used for each planning object.
claims.quote: For each planning object in the forecast, it shows which demand forecasting algorithm was used and the resulting SMAPE value.

claims.where: summary; What's changing
claims.claim: The page shows the resulting SMAPE value for each planning object.
claims.quote: For each planning object in the forecast, it shows which demand forecasting algorithm was used and the resulting SMAPE value.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: SMAPE stands for symmetric mean absolute percentage error.
claims.quote: The *Best fit model - version 4* forecasting algorithm introduces symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) as the new metric for selecting between forecast models.

claims.where: What's changing: SMAPE parenthesis
claims.claim: SMAPE measures forecast accuracy through errors relative to observed demand.
claims.quote: **SMAPE** metric. Returns the symmetric mean absolute percentage error metric, an accuracy measure based on percentage errors.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/office/vba/api/excel.worksheetfunction.forecast_ets_stat#remarks to sources for the plain-language SMAPE definition, or remove the parenthetical definition.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The calculation accuracy page adds a model distribution visualization.
claims.quote: New data visualizations include model distribution and an average SMAPE indicator that responds to filters.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The average SMAPE indicator responds to filters.
claims.quote: New data visualizations include model distribution and an average SMAPE indicator that responds to filters.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The page improves on the explainability display previously available in forecast profile job run history.
claims.quote: The new calculation accuracy page for forecast time series improves on the explainability display previously available in the forecast profile job run history.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Planners can drill into individual planning objects such as a product and store.
claims.quote: The calculation accuracy page also lets you drill down into individual planning objects (such as product and store) for an even more detailed explainability view.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The detailed view presents historical data alongside each calculated forecast.
claims.quote: Here, you can see historical data alongside each calculated forecast and get a natural-language explanation of the factors driving it.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The detailed view supplies a natural-language explanation of forecast drivers.
claims.quote: Here, you can see historical data alongside each calculated forecast and get a natural-language explanation of the factors driving it.

claims.where: title; summary; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The forecast explanations are AI-generated.
claims.quote: Understand forecast drivers through AI-generated explanations.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Version 1.4 adds Best fit model - version 4, using SMAPE to choose between forecast models.
claims.quote: The *Best fit model - version 4* forecasting algorithm introduces symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) as the new metric for selecting between forecast models.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Version 1.4 adds a forecast breakdown into baseline, signals impact and manual adjustments.
claims.quote: Demand planning splits each forecast into *baseline*, *signals impact*, and *manual adjustments* to provide clearer insight into manual changes and the influence of signals.

claims.where: What's changing: final paragraph
claims.claim: Learn lists this capability in a released version, unlike the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: This article lists new features, fixes, improvements, and known issues for each released version of Demand planning in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The supplied roadmap and Learn description describe accuracy displays and explanations, not autonomous forecast changes.
claims.quote: Searched: Demand planning calculation accuracy detailed forecast explainability AI explanations enable disable setting security role Dataverse table API. Read roadmap and what's-new version 1.4: displays, explanations and a separate component breakdown, no forecast-changing action by explanations.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No UI or API switch specifically governing the calculation accuracy page's AI forecast explanations is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Demand planning explainability disable; Demand planning forecast explainability setting Dataverse Web API entity reference enable. Opened what's-new, demand-planning-copilot, enable-copilot and install-demand-planning; no switch for these explanations found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Copilot for demand planning setting's documented feature is Analyze demand plans with Copilot, not the new accuracy explanations.
claims.quote: Searched: Demand planning explainability disable. Opened demand-planning-copilot and enable-copilot: setting procedure explicitly names Analyze demand plans with Copilot; neither connects it to calculation accuracy explanations in what's-new version 1.4.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn names no security role specific to the calculation accuracy page.
claims.quote: Searched: calculation accuracy security Demand planning; Demand planning calculation accuracy detailed forecast explainability AI explanations enable disable setting security role Dataverse table API. Opened users-access and what's-new: app roles but no page-specific role.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe the generation mechanism specific to the new forecast explanations.
claims.quote: Searched: Demand planning detailed forecast explainability responsible AI data processing region model. Opened what's-new, enable-copilot, faq-demand-planning-copilot and faq-demand-planning-generative-insights; no mechanism for the new calculation accuracy explanations.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not specify the forecast data sent to an AI model for these explanations.
claims.quote: Searched: Demand planning detailed forecast explainability responsible AI data processing region model. Read what's-new and both Demand planning Responsible AI FAQs; they do not identify the model payload for calculation accuracy explanations.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not specify where the calculation accuracy explanation's AI processing occurs.
claims.quote: Searched: Demand planning detailed forecast explainability responsible AI data processing region model. Opened what's-new, enable-copilot and the two Demand planning Responsible AI FAQs; none specifies a processing region for these explanations.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Contributors without the Manager or System Administrator role can view and edit only data granted through row-level access rules.
claims.quote: Users who have the *Demand Planning Contributor* role (but not *Demand Planning Manager* or *System Administrator*) can access Demand planning, but they can only view and edit data that they're granted access to.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Those demand planning contributors see no data by default until a row-level rule grants access.
claims.quote: By default, demand planning contributors can't see any data until they're granted access to it by a row-level access rule.

claims.where: Scope: Who; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Access requires a Power Platform user account with the security roles for the needed features.
claims.quote: To be able to access Demand planning, users must sign in a Power Platform user account that has the security roles for the features they need.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1]; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Demand Planning Contributor grants access to Demand planning.
claims.quote:
**Demand Planning Contributor**

- This role is added when you install Demand planning.
- Grants access to Demand planing.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1]; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Demand Planning Manager grants access to Demand planning.
claims.quote:
**Demand Planning Manager**

- This role is added when you install Demand planning.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1]
claims.claim: System Administrator grants access to Demand planning.

**System Administrator**

- Grants access to Demand planning and all features that are available to the *Demand Planning Manager*, *Demand Planning Contributor*, and *Basic User* roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing: Indirect costs
claims.claim: New installations and updates to version 1.4 might require significantly more processing time than previous versions.
claims.quote: As a result of these preparations, both new installations and updates to version 1.4 might require significantly more processing time than previous versions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The longer installation and update processing comes from engineering preparations for Dataverse storage alignment.
claims.quote: This release includes behind-the-scenes enhancements that prepare the app to support Dataverse storage for timeseries data. As a result of these preparations, both new installations and updates to version 1.4 might require significantly more processing time than previous versions.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Demand planning is installed through the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Follow these steps to install Demand planning in Power Platform admin center.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Demand planning must be installed on the same tenant as Supply Chain Management for built-in import and export profiles.
claims.quote: You must install Demand planning on the same tenant as your Supply Chain Management environment to ensure that the built-in import and export profiles can be used to import and export data.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Demand planning cannot be installed in the tenant's default environment.
claims.quote: Due to a current technical limitation, you can't install Demand planning on your tenant's default environment.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Supported Supply Chain Management versions include 10.0.36 build 10.0.1695.83 or later, or another version and build listed by the installation page.
claims.quote:
Supply Chain Management version 10.0.36, build 10.0.1695.83 or later
- Supply Chain Management version 10.0.37, build 10.0.1725.60 or later

claims.where: Scope: Version; Open questions
claims.claim: A version 1.4 rollout schedule for existing Demand planning environments is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Demand planning version 1.4 release rollout schedule availability date; Demand planning 1.4 release. Opened what's-new and manage-apps; neither dates version 1.4 environment rollout. Returned database-migration schedule concerns storage migration, not version 1.4.

claims.where: controls[1].ui
claims.claim: Direct user security roles are managed in Power Platform admin center through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote: Select Manage. In the Manage pane, select Environments, and then select an environment from the list. Select Settings. Select Users + permissions, and then select Users. On the Users page select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.where: controls[1].api; controls[1].note
claims.claim: The printed v9.0 POST systemuserroles_association/$ref call assigns a role to the identified user, with the role supplied as @odata.id.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope: Roles that manage access
claims.claim: Assigning security roles requires at least Read and Assign privileges on the Security Role table.
claims.quote: To assign security roles to a user, you need to have the appropriate privileges (minimum privileges are **Read** and **Assign** on the **Security Role** table).

claims.where: Scope: Roles that manage access
claims.claim: System Administrator has the required security-role assignment privileges by default.
claims.quote: By default, the System Administrator security role has all the required privileges to assign security roles to any user, including assigning the System Administrator security role.

claims.where: controls[2].ui
claims.claim: Licences can be assigned through Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.where: controls[2].api
claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense with UserId, AddLicenses containing SkuId, and empty RemoveLicenses assigns the specified licence.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.

Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[2].note; Scope: Roles that manage access
claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.where: Governance controls: Copilot for demand planning path
claims.claim: The Power Apps maker portal route is Solutions > Default Solution > Settings > Copilot for demand planning.
claims.quote: In the Objects list, select Settings. In the Copilot for demand planning row, select the link in the Display name column. In the Edit Copilot for demand planning dialog box, in the Setting environment value section, select Add existing value.
claims.fix: Complete the background setting path as 'Solutions > Default Solution > Objects > Settings > Copilot for demand planning > Setting environment value > Add existing value > Yes/No', selecting the target environment first. Keep its applicability limited to Analyze demand plans with Copilot.

claims.where: Governance controls: Copilot for demand planning
claims.claim: The environment setting turns Analyze demand plans with Copilot on or off.
claims.quote: In the dropdown list, select *Yes* to enable the feature for the current environment, or select *No* to disable it.

claims.where: Governance controls: Copilot for demand planning
claims.claim: Analyze demand plans with Copilot is on by default.
claims.quote: The *Analyze demand plans with Copilot* feature is on by default.

claims.where: Governance controls: Copilot for demand planning
claims.claim: A system administrator of the environment must change the Analyze demand plans with Copilot setting.
claims.quote: A system administrator of the environment must complete this procedure.

claims.where: Governance controls: Publish bots with AI features
claims.claim: The Publish bots with AI features setting is found under Settings in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Open Power Platform admin center. On the navigation pane, select Settings. In the list, select the row where the Name field is set to Publish bots with AI features.

claims.where: Governance controls: Publish bots with AI features
claims.claim: Publish bots with AI features is a tenant-level setting.
claims.quote: By default, the tenant-level setting that enables the deployment of Copilot bots in Dataverse environments is enabled.

claims.where: Governance controls: Publish bots with AI features
claims.claim: Publish bots with AI features is enabled by default.
claims.quote: By default, the tenant-level setting that enables the deployment of Copilot bots in Dataverse environments is enabled.

claims.where: Governance controls: Publish bots with AI features
claims.claim: Learn states that disabling this tenant setting prevents use of Copilot features in finance and operations apps.
claims.quote: However, a tenant admin can disable this setting. If the setting is disabled, you can't use Copilot features in finance and operations apps.

claims.quote: Searched: Demand planning explainability disable; Demand planning forecast explainability setting Dataverse Web API entity reference enable. Read demand-planning-copilot, enable-copilot and what's-new: broader scopes are stated, but neither identifies this new explanation feature.
